content: The Prairie State Achievement Examination (PSAE) is a standardized test administered over two days to all high school juniors in Illinois. This examination has been a mandatory requirement for all Illinois high school students since 2001. The PSAE evaluates students in the following subject areas: Mathematics Reading Science Writing A student is required to take the PSAE in order to earn a high school diploma unless they meet one of the following exemption criteria: 1. The student’s Individualized Education Program (IEP) is incompatible with the PSAE, and the test cannot be modified to accommodate their needs. In such cases, the student takes the Illinois Alternate Assessment instead. 2. The student is not proficient in English. In this scenario, the student takes the Illinois Measure of Annual Growth in English instead. 3. The student is enrolled in an alternative education program, such as an adult education program or a high school equivalency certificate program. For the 2006-2007 school year, a student may be exempted from the PSAE if they meet one of the following conditions: 1. The student has taken the ACT after their freshman year and achieved reportable scores. 2. The student is a senior and meets one of the following criteria: They have taken an alternative form of testing. They were eligible for a medical exemption during the 2005-2006 examination. They were incarcerated during both the 2005-2006 and 2006-2007 examination periods. They are a transfer student who transferred after May 1, 2006.
